name: Fibromuscular Dysplasia of the Coronary Arteries

criteria.description: Characteristic angiographic appearance of multifocal or focal coronary artery stenosis with a 'string-of-beads' or smooth tubular narrowing
Exclusion of atherosclerotic coronary artery disease by clinical, imaging, and laboratory evaluation
Histopathologic or imaging evidence supporting noninflammatory and nonatherosclerotic arterial wall changes
Presence of fibromuscular dysplasia in other vascular beds (e.g., renal or carotid arteries)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic angiographic pattern with exclusion of atherosclerosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on coronary angiography combined with exclusion of other causes of coronary artery stenosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Often precipitates acute coronary syndrome in young patients without traditional risk factors

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multifocal coronary artery stenosis with 'string-of-beads' appearance
searchTerms: multiple coronary artery narrowings with beads
string of beads pattern in heart arteries

common.notes: Due to myocardial ischemia from coronary artery stenosis

occasional.notes: Due to transient ischemia or arrhythmia

occasional.symptomName: Headache related to associated cerebrovascular FMD
searchTerms: headache linked to brain blood vessel disease

occasional.symptomName: Hypertension secondary to renal artery involvement
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney artery
secondary high blood pressure from kidneys

rare.notes: Rarely detected in associated vascular beds
searchTerms: swollen blood vessels in arms or legs

imaging: Coronary angiography showing multifocal stenosis with 'string-of-beads' pattern
Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) or optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating arterial wall abnormalities
CT angiography or MR angiography for extracoronary vessel assessment
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; possible familial clustering reported
other: Histopathology showing medial fibroplasia with alternating areas of stenosis and aneurysmal dilatation
Exclusion of vasculitis and atherosclerosis by clinical and laboratory evaluation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of traditional cardiovascular risk factors
Systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss
Histopathologic evidence of vessel wall inflammation
Imaging showing intimal flap or intramural hematoma
May occur in absence of FMD

redFlags: Acute myocardial infarction in young patients without risk factors
Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained syncope
references: Olin JW, Gornik HL, Bacharach JM, et al. Fibromuscular Dysplasia: State of the Science and Critical Unanswered Questions: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2014;129(9):1048-1078.

Saw J. Coronary Artery Spontaneous Dissection. Can J Cardiol. 2013;29(9):1027-1033.
